executive_assessment.text: The July 2026 WFP account documents differentiated food-access burdens and a women-managed grain bank in Uriles Pinalón, Jalapa; one case does not establish prevalence across the Dry Corridor.
The UN programme identifies seven target municipalities and intended food/water resilience capacities. Targets are not achieved results; the IPC estimate retained here is historical and national.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-07-16 reports: WFP reports that climate variability compounded by El Niño is reducing Dry Corridor harvests and food access, with women bearing a disproportionate household food-allocation burden.

Source dated 2026-07-16 reports: In Uriles Pinalón, Jalapa, a woman farmer described late, insufficient rain and poor milpa yields; WFP says women in rural Indigenous communities, including Ch’orti’-speaking areas, often reduce their own food portions for household members.

Source dated 2026-07-16 reports: WFP reports installing a CERF-supported grain bank and silo in Uriles Pinalón; local women organize and manage the grain, reducing the need for households to travel to town to buy maize and beans.

Source dated not stated reports: The UN joint programme targets more than 7,000 households, especially children under five and pregnant or lactating women, in seven Dry Corridor municipalities across Chiquimula and Jalapa: Jocotán, Camotán, Olopa, San Juan Ermita, Chiquimula, San Luis Jilotepeque and San Pedro Pinula.

Source dated not stated reports: The project profile identifies irregular rainfall, drought, floods, landslides, environmental degradation and low crop yields in its Dry Corridor context; it reports that Indigenous people, especially women and children, are disproportionately affected by poverty and social exclusion.

Source dated not stated reports: Planned outputs include drought-adapted food systems, community water infrastructure and watershed planning with women's participation, plus stronger central and local capacity for food and water security and gender-responsive resilience.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 7 of 7 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
Searches did not find a directly inspected Guatemala primary passage explicitly linking the climate and food-security pressures documented here to violence, armed conflict or displacement.
The July–September 2026 food-security projections in the government/IPC sources had elapsed by 27 October 2026; realized outcomes were not verified.
The Guatemala 2025 Biennial Transparency Report could not be opened because the official PDF redirect looped; its search listing was not used as evidence.
Expired July–September forecasts are excluded; the October 2026–February 2027 outlook is not treated as an observed 2026 outcome.
The named grain-bank example and joint-programme geography add local context, but no supported climate→violence or reverse insecurity-to-adaptation mechanism was retrieved.
